title: Affine blowup chart presentation for a regular sequence
statement: Let $R$ be a ring and let $a,a_2,\ldots,a_s$ be a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Put $I=(a,a_2,\ldots,a_s)$ and let $R[I/a]$ be the affine blowup chart [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring]. Then $R[I/a]$ is canonically isomorphic to $R[y_2,\ldots,y_s]/(a y_i-a_i\mid 2\le i\le s)$, with $y_i$ corresponding to $a_i/a$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 0BIQ (lemma-blowup-regular-sequence), statement and proof

proof.text: Put $S=R[y_2,\ldots,y_s]$, $f_1=a$ and $f_i=a_i$ for $2\le i\le s$, regarded as constant polynomials in $S$. Put $J=(ay_i-a_i\mid2\le i\le s)$ and $Q=S/J$. Apply [lem-trf-polynomial-regular-sequence-syzygies] to the given ordered sequence in $R$, with $m=s-1$ and $z_{i-1}=y_i$. Thus every relation $\sum f_iv_i=0$ in $S^s$ is a sum of the vectors $f_ie_j-f_je_i$.

source.place: Tag 0BIQ, polynomial-extension H_1 argument, realized by the polynomial syzygy lemma.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-koszul-relations-quotient-torsionfree] over $S$, with the constant $f_i$ above and $t_i=y_i$. Step 1 gives its syzygy hypothesis. Its ideal $(f_1t_i-f_i\mid2\le i\le s)$ equals $J$, so its quotient is the same $Q$. Thus multiplication by $a$ on $Q$ is injective. Explicitly, if $a^Nx=0$, induction on $N$ gives $x=0$: for $N=0$ this is the hypothesis itself, and for $N+1$ injectivity first gives $a^Nx=0$.

source.place: Tag 0BIQ, final torsion-free inference, realized by the syzygy-saturation lemma.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-blowup-chart-presentation-power-torsion] over the original ring $R$, to the generators $a,a_2,\ldots,a_s$ of $I$. Its polynomial quotient is precisely $Q$. It gives a surjective $R$-algebra map $\phi:Q\to R[I/a]\subseteq R_a$ sending $[y_i]$ to $a_i/a$. Its kernel consists exactly of classes killed by some power of $a$. Each such class is zero by Step 2, so $\phi$ is injective as well as surjective. This uses no invertibility of $a$ in $Q$.

source.place: Tag 0G8S, quotient-description and power-torsion kernel; Tag 0BIQ, opening reduction.

proof.text: For $b\in R[I/a]$ let $\psi(b)$ be the unique $x\in Q$ with $\phi(x)=b$, which exists by Step 3. Applying $\phi$ shows $\psi(b+c)=\psi(b)+\psi(c)$ and $\psi(bc)=\psi(b)\psi(c)$; injectivity gives these identities, and similarly preservation of $1$ and the image of every $r\in R$. Thus $\psi$ is an $R$-algebra inverse to $\phi$. For uniqueness, any $R$-algebra map $Q\to R[I/a]$ with the asserted variable images agrees with $\phi$ after the polynomial quotient map by [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]; that quotient map is surjective, so the maps agree. This proves the canonical isomorphism with the required generator images. For $s=1$ there are no variables or relations, $Q=R$, Step 1 has $m=0$, and Steps 2-3 still prove that the chart map is bijective.
